channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Messias defende aprimorar STF e autocontenção em pautas polêmicas
item.description: Jorge Messias, nominated to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) by President Lula, argued during his Senate CCJ hearing that the STF must continuously improve and exercise self-restraint on divisive issues, emphasizing transparency, ethics, and institutional control to strengthen democracy and counter authoritarian discourses. Although identifying as evangelical, he reaffirmed his commitment to a secular state and stressed that all powers must be subject to rules in a republic.

item.title: Messias diz que STF não deve ser “Procon da política”
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), stated that the Court should not act as a 'consumer protection agency for politics,' emphasizing judicial self-restraint, respect for the Legislative and Executive branches, and the duty to uphold the Constitution without overstepping or omitting action when constitutional violations occur. Regarding the January 8, 2023 attacks, he described them as 'one of the saddest episodes' of his life, clarified that the AGU requested arrests in flagrante (not preventive), and affirmed he acted within his constitutional duty to defend public federal property, while avoiding individual case commentary to prevent prejudgment.

item.title: STF “não deve ser protagonista”, diz Jorge Messias em sabatina
item.description: Jorge Messias, nominee to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), stated that the Court should not play a protagonist role in the political system but exercise self-restraint, guaranteeing fundamental rights and preserving the Constitution without replacing Congress’s function. He argued the Judiciary should play a residual and complementary role in public policy, exercising moderation in restricting rights like freedom of expression, and stressed judicial ethics, collegial decision-making, and adherence to legislative rules to prevent judicial voluntarism. Messias also emphasized transparency, accountability, and societal dialogue as essential to maintaining the Court’s credibility.

item.title: Ministério da Justiça cobra da gestão Tarcísio envio de dados sobre homicídios e estatísticas da segurança pública em SP
item.description: The Ministry of Justice has issued a formal notice to São Paulo’s Public Security Secretary demanding the urgent submission of March 2026 crime statistics, which remain outstanding and are blocking the consolidation of national crime data for the first quarter. The deadline for compliance is May 5, after which the state may be deemed non-compliant with the National Public Security Information System (Sinesp), risking suspension of federal security funds and judicial action. The Tarcísio de Freitas administration is accused of systematically delaying such data submissions.

item.title: Crusoé: Messias se posiciona como o ministro ‘terrivelmente evangélico’ de Lula
item.description: Attorney General Jorge Messias positioned himself as Lula's 'terribly evangelical' minister for the STF during his Senate CCJ hearing, echoing a phrase first used by Jair Bolsonaro when nominating André Mendonça. The statement reflects an effort to align Lula's government with evangelical voters through judicially appointed figures who uphold conservative values.

item.title: De olho em votos da bancada evangélica, Messias se compromete com ‘valores espirituais que o norteiam’
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias, nominated by Lula to the STF, pledged to act according to Christian and evangelical values, stating his faith guides him without violating state secularism. He advocated for judicial impartiality, inter-branch harmony, and a complementary role for the Supreme Court vis-à-vis Congress, rejecting the idea of exclusive constitutional interpretation by the Judiciary.

item.title: Messias recebe políticos e pastor evangélico em sala reservada antes de sabatina no Senado
item.description: Jorge Messias, head of the Attorney General's Office and nominee to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), received greetings from allies, former ministers, lawmakers, and Pastor Samuel Câmara of the Assembleia de Deus in a restricted Senate room before his confirmation hearing in the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ). He arrived accompanied by Defense Minister José Múcio and was welcomed by PSB and PT leaders, AGU officials, and his family. Messias avoided press questions, saying only 'Glória a Deus' as he entered the hearing, with allies describing him as calm and confident about the outcome.

item.title: Governo amplia em R$ 5 bilhões crédito a exportadores afetados por tarifas dos EUA e guerra no Oriente Médio
item.description: The federal government expanded by R$ 5 billion the extraordinary credit line for Brazilian exporters affected by U.S. tariffs and the Middle East war, through a provisional measure strengthening the Export Guarantee Fund (FGE) under the Brazil Sovereign Plan. The funds support individuals and companies, including suppliers, with priority given to high-tech strategic sectors. The measure takes effect immediately but requires congressional approval within 120 days to remain valid.

item.title: O argumento do relator de indicação de Messias para convencer oposição
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, sought to persuade the opposition by arguing that the vote should not be used to defeat President Lula, but to assess the nomination with conscience. He stated that those wishing to oppose Lula can do so in the October elections, and that rejecting the nomination would be unfair to end the career of a young professional prematurely.

item.title: Leia íntegra da fala de Jorge Messias em sabatina no Senado
item.description: Attorney General Jorge Messias delivered his opening remarks during the Senate hearing for his STF nomination, emphasizing his professional background, commitment to the Court, and personal convictions, including his evangelical faith and opposition to abortion. He became emotional at times and thanked officials from all branches of government, while representing the OAB and other government nominees. Approval requires a simple majority in the CCJ.

item.title: Minha identidade é evangélica, mas o Estado é laico, diz Messias
item.description: Attorney General Jorge Messias stated during his Senate CCJ hearing that while his identity is evangelical, the state must remain secular, emphasizing that constitutional judges must be loyal to the Constitution, not personal religious convictions. He spoke emotionally about his evangelical upbringing and said Christian principles guide him, as long as laicity is respected. Nominated by Lula for the STF, Messias must be approved by the CCJ and then secure at least 41 votes in the Senate’s secret ballot.

item.title: Oposição vê ‘não’ a Jorge Messias como o impeachment possível a ministros do STF
item.description: Opposition senators are framing the rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF as a symbolic 'impeachment' of Supreme Court ministers, citing the Court’s reputational crisis, alleged ties between ministers and banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Lula’s weakened political standing in Congress. Messias’ confirmation hearing has begun, with senators like Roberta Acioly (Republicanos-RR) issuing statements against his nomination, arguing the STF should not serve as an extension of political power. Lula delayed the formal submission of the nomination by four months after announcing it in November 2025, as a strategy to build support amid Senate resistance.

item.title: Messias repete fala de Moraes em sabatina de 2017 ao defender contenção do Judiciário
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union, Jorge Messias, defended the improvement of the STF and stated that all branches of power must be subject to checks, repeating a statement he made in 2017 during a confirmation hearing. The remark was made at a press briefing on Wednesday, April 29, 2026.

item.title: As 'vacinas' jurídicas de Flávio Bolsonaro contra ofensiva do PT sobre caso Master
item.description: The PT showed a video at its national congress linking Flávio Bolsonaro to the Banco Master scandal, calling him 'the most corrupt son' of Jair Bolsonaro and dubbing the case 'bolsomaster'. However, the senator is not under investigation for involvement in Daniel Vorcaro’s irregularities, as clarified in the exclusive article.

item.title: Messias defende STF ‘aberto ao aperfeiçoamento’ e sem excessos: ‘Nem ativismo, nem passivismo’
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the STF, advocated for a Supreme Court open to improvement, rejecting both judicial activism and passivity in favor of balance among the branches and judicial ethics as the foundation of democracy. He stressed collegiality as key to preserving the Court's legitimacy and positioned Congress as the central force in institutional equilibrium.

item.title: Messias chega a sabatina com expectativa de aprovação apertada e discurso de 'pacificador' no STF
item.description: Jorge Messias, minister of the Advocacy-General of the Union, faces a Senate hearing for his nomination to the STF, with expectations of a close vote despite government and STF allies expressing confidence in his approval. He positions himself as a 'pacifier,' aiming to mediate between the court's internal factions without formally aligning with any bloc, while emphasizing his evangelical identity and commitment to a secular state.

item.title: Gaspar chama Lindbergh de criminoso e pede cassação: “Seja homem”
item.description: Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) called Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) a 'criminal' during a Chamber speech, after Farias and Senator Soraya Thronicke accused him of rape of a vulnerable minor and cover-up in a case involving a 13-year-old girl in Alagoas from about 9 years ago. Gaspar demanded Farias's mandate be cassated for breach of decorum and released a DNA test to defend himself, while the accusers filed a PF investigation request with secrecy and evidence preservation measures.

item.title: A variação na popularidade de Tarcísio, a 5 meses da eleição em São Paulo
item.description: A Quaest poll conducted between April 23 and 27, 2026, shows that Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' approval rating dropped from 60% in August 2025 to 54% currently, while disapproval remained stable at 29%. Positive government evaluation fell from 45% to 39%, and negative evaluation rose from 15% to 19%. 54% of voters believe he deserves re-election, down from 56% in August last year.

item.title: Sabatina de Messias na CCJ: 'Minha identidade é evangélica, mas tenho clareza de que o Estado é laico'
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the STF, stated during his CCJ hearing that while his identity is evangelical, he upholds the secular nature of the State as a constitutional principle, advocating for constructive dialogue between the State and all religions. He also discussed moral issues such as the right to life and family protection, linking them to the Federal Constitution. His career includes leading the AGU since 2023, focusing on defending democratic institutions and advancing key government agendas.

item.title: Messias declara apoio a debate no Congresso sobre decisões individuais de ministros do STF
item.description: Jorge Messias, nominated by President Lula to the STF, advocated in a Senate CCJ hearing for collegial decision-making at the Supreme Court, criticizing individual (monocratic) rulings as undermining the Court's institutional dimension. He praised Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco and Senator Davi Alcolumbre for supporting congressional debate on limiting individual ministerial decisions, stating that Congress is the essential space for political mediation and inter-branch pacification.

item.title: Relator da indicação de Messias espera 16 votos favoráveis na CCJ
item.description: The rapporteur for Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF, Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), said he expects 16 favorable votes in the CCJ — two above the minimum — and 48 in the plenary, seven above the required threshold. He aims to speed up the hearing by asking allied senators to shorten their speeches to avoid a session lasting up to 13 hours, citing secret voting and political polarization as obstacles to precise vote mapping.

item.title: Messias cobra transparência do STF e fala em “ajuste de rotas”
item.description: Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias stated during his CCJ Senate hearing that the Supreme Federal Court (STF) must expand transparency mechanisms and remain open to institutional improvement, referencing the need for a 'course adjustment'. Nominated by President Lula for an STF vacancy, Messias emphasized that the Court should modernize without compromising its independence.

item.title: ACM Neto e Jerônimo têm empate técnico na disputa pelo governo da Bahia, aponta Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows a technical tie between former Salvador mayor ACM Neto (Union Brazil) and incumbent Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) in the Bahia gubernatorial race, with both candidates within the margin of error. Released on Wednesday (29), the survey highlights high rejection rates for both and a substantial share of undecided voters or those planning to cast blank/null ballots.

item.title: Mesmo liderando disputa ao governo, aprovação a Tarcísio tem menor patamar em dois anos
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) has seen his approval rating in São Paulo drop to 54%, the lowest in two years, with notable declines among women, young voters aged 16–24, and seniors over 60. Despite this, he remains the frontrunner in re-election polls and could win in the first round. The Genial/Quaest survey, conducted from April 23–27 with 1,650 respondents, has a 95% confidence level and a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre recebe enxurrada de ligações por Messias, mas não atende chamados
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre received numerous calls from supporters of Jorge Messias and those seeking to mitigate the fallout from the leak of his meeting with the AGU minister at Justice Cristiano Zanin’s residence. Despite the outreach, Alcolumbre ignored most calls on the eve of Messias’ CCJ hearing. The incident highlights political tensions surrounding the Supreme Court nomination process.

item.title: Aliado do governo, relator da indicação de Messias ao STF calcula 45 votos pela aprovação
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, projects 45 favorable votes in the plenary, with at least 16 in the CCJ. The government base seeks to limit the hearing time to avoid overexposure, while allies expect approval but with a narrow margin. The vote is seen as a gauge of Lula’s relationship with the Senate, particularly due to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s public neutrality.

item.title: Indicado ao STF, Messias chega à CCJ para sabatina: “Deus abençoe”
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union, Jorge Messias, arrived at the Senate for a hearing in the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) regarding his nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), following his selection by President Lula to replace the retired Minister Luís Roberto Barroso. When asked about expectations, he simply replied, 'God bless everyone,' accompanied by his wife, Karina Messias. The hearing marks the first step in the confirmation process, requiring CCJ approval and later at least 41 favorable votes in the Senate plenary in a secret vote.

item.title: Senado começa sessão de sabatina de Messias ao STF, e governistas preveem placar apertado
item.description: The sabatina of Attorney General Jorge Messias for the STF began in the Senate, with government allies predicting approval but a tight vote due to uncertainty among undecided senators. The vote is seen as a barometer of Lula’s relationship with Congress, particularly amid tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who has not taken a public stance. Despite 25 confirmed favorable votes, Messias needs at least 16 of the 34 undecided senators to reach the 41-vote threshold, with allies banking on silent support in the secret ballot.

item.title: O bispo que pode servir de guia para Flávio Bolsonaro entre eleitores católicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro plans to attend a religious event alongside Bishop Dom Adair José de Moraes from the Diocese of Formosa (GO) to strengthen his support among Catholic voters, a demographic where he trails Lula. The bishop is known for his criticism of the Lula government and gained viral attention for opposing a Carnival parade that honored the president. The move is seen as a valuable first step by Bolsonaro allies, including evangelicals, to connect with Catholic voters.

item.title: Messias chega ao Senado para sabatina por vaga no STF acompanhado de Múcio e de ex-ministro Jader Filho
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias arrived at the Senate for his confirmation hearing for a Supreme Court vacancy, accompanied by Defense Minister José Múcio and former Cities Minister Jader Filho. The vote remains uncertain, with 25 favorable, 22 opposed, and 34 senators undecided or unwilling to state their position publicly; Messias needs at least 16 of these to reach the 41 votes required for approval. The government projects 44–49 votes, relying on secret ballot to reduce political cost, while the lack of public stance by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre sustains tension between the Executive and Legislative branches.

item.title: Jorge Messias passa por sabatina no Senado para vaga no STF; acompanhe ao vivo
item.description: Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union, is undergoing a Senate CCJ hearing for a Supreme Court vacancy, nominated by President Lula. He needs at least 14 votes in the CCJ and 41 in the full Senate to be approved. The vote takes place amid political tension between the government and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who supports another candidate.

item.title: Aliado do governo, presidente da CCJ do Senado vê clima 'favorável' para a aprovação de Messias ao STF
item.description: The president of the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee, Otto Alencar (PSD-BA), says he sees a favorable climate for the approval of Jorge Messias to the STF, though the vote in the plenary is expected to be tight. The government has 25 confirmed favorable votes and 22 opposed, needing to win at least 16 of the 34 undecided or non-committed senators to reach the 41 required. The vote is seen as a gauge of Lula's relationship with Congress, especially amid tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and following the Flávio Dino nomination, which received fewer votes than projected.

item.title: ACM Neto e Jerônimo empatam em disputa pelo governo da Bahia
item.description: ACM Neto and Jerônimo Rodrigues are tied in the Bahia gubernatorial race, with Neto leading in both first-round (41% vs 36-37%) and second-round (41% vs 38%) scenarios. Jerônimo has the highest rejection rate at 42%, despite 56% of Bahians approving his administration. The Quaest poll, with a 3-point margin of error and TSE registration BA-03657/2026, surveyed 1,200 people across 61 municipalities from April 23–27, 2026.

item.title: Ao vivo: CCJ sabatina Jorge Messias para vaga no STF
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee is holding a hearing this Wednesday (April 29, 2026) starting at 9 a.m. for Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union, nominated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to fill the Supreme Federal Court vacancy left by Justice Roberto Barroso. The live broadcast is available via the provided link.

item.title: Os números da disputa entre Tarcísio e Haddad em SP, segundo a Quaest
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas leads the re-election race in São Paulo, with a 12-point advantage over Fernando Haddad in the first round and 17 points in a potential runoff, according to a Quaest/Genial Investimentos poll. He could win in the first round, as his support exceeds the combined totals of his opponents in both scenarios tested. The survey interviewed 1,650 voters between April 23 and 27, with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: STF retoma julgamento sobre desoneração da folha de pagamentos
item.description: The STF resumed the judgment on the constitutionality of the 2023 payroll tax exemption extension, which replaces the 20% employer social security contribution with 1% to 4.5% on gross revenue for 17 labor-intensive sectors. Rapporteur Minister Cristiano Zanin voted to strike down the law due to lack of budgetary compensation and fiscal sustainability, a position supported by Ministers Edson Fachin and Gilmar Mendes, while Alexandre de Moraes requested a view, pausing the proceedings. The 2024 agreement between the government and Congress for gradual reinstatement from 2025 to 2027 was not considered, as it is not part of the case.

item.title: Sabatina do BESSIAS: Papéis TROCADOS + Antipetista vs Antissistema + Flávio vs Lula: Eleições 2026.
item.description: The BESSIAS interview featured an unusual dynamic with reversed roles between interviewers and interviewees, highlighting the clash between anti-PT and anti-system forces. The confrontation between Flávio and Lula emerged as central to the 2026 elections, reflecting ideological polarization and campaign strategies focused on governance and systemic change.

item.title: Quaest: 54% aprovam e 29% desaprovam governo Tarcísio de Freitas em São Paulo
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' approval rating in São Paulo dropped from 60% to 54% since August 2025, according to a Quaest poll released in April 2026. Despite the decline, 54% of voters still approve of his administration, while 29% disapprove. The survey also shows 54% of São Paulo residents believe he deserves re-election, compared to 36% who do not.

item.title: Lula se reúne com governadores no Palácio do Planalto nesta quarta-feira, 29
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will meet with two governors on Wednesday, the 29th, at the Planalto Palace. At 3 p.m., he will receive the interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, Ricardo Couto, who replaced Cláudio Castro after his resignation. At 4 p.m., he will meet with the governor of Bahia, Jerônimo Rodrigues, from the PT.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Tarcísio lidera contra Haddad em São Paulo com vantagem de 12 pontos
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 38% of voting intentions, against 26% for Fernando Haddad (PT), a 12-point advantage. In a scenario excluding Paulo Serra (PSDB), the lead remains at 12 points (40% to 28%). Tarcísio also beats Haddad in a simulated runoff by 49% to 32%. The survey indicates volatility, with 50% of voters saying their vote could change.

item.title: Pesquisa: candidata de Lula lidera disputa pelo Senado em São Paulo
item.description: Former Planning Minister Simone Tebet (PSB) leads the Senate race in São Paulo with 14-15% voting intentions, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. Former Entrepreneurship Minister Marcio França (PSB) follows with 12%, technically tied with Tebet and former Environment Minister Marina Silva (Rede), who also reaches 12% in an alternate scenario. Meanwhile, Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leads the gubernatorial race with potential to win in the first round.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Haddad tem 58% de rejeição em SP; 38% não votariam em Tarcísio
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Fernando Haddad (PT) with 58% rejection, the highest among São Paulo gubernatorial candidates, while 38% say they would not vote for Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). Tarcísio leads in vote potential at 48%, followed by Haddad at 33%, Paulo Serra (PSDB) at 9%, and Kim Kataguiri (Missão) at 8%. Haddad's rejection is particularly strong among Bolsonarists (80%) and non-Bolsonarist right (88%), while Tarcísio is rejected by 73% of non-Lulist left and 62% of Lulists.

item.title: Tarcísio tem chance de se reeleger governador de SP no 1º turno, aponta Quaest
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas leads voting intentions for the 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial election, with 38% to 40% in two first-round scenarios, suggesting a potential first-round victory. His main rival, Fernando Haddad (PT), trails at 26% to 28%, while Kim Kataguiri and Paulo Serra each stand at 5%. In a simulated runoff, Tarcísio would win with 49% against Haddad’s 32%.

item.title: Pesquisa Genial/Quaest: Avaliação do governo Tarcísio piora, puxada pelas mulheres, mas maioria quer reeleição
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' approval rating dropped from 60% to 54% in São Paulo, with the sharpest decline among women and across all age and income groups, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. Despite declining approval, 54% of voters still support his re-election, and he leads Fernando Haddad by 12 points in the gubernatorial race.

item.title: Governo de Tarcísio é aprovado por 54% em São Paulo
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on April 29, 2026, shows that Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) has a 54% approval rating and 29% disapproval in São Paulo. He leads the first-round voting intentions for the 2026 elections with 38% to 40%, followed by Fernando Haddad (PT) at 26% to 28%. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio would defeat Haddad 49% to 32%.

item.title: Tarcísio lidera em SP com 38% contra 26% de Haddad
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas leading the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 38% of voting intentions in the first round, against 26% for Fernando Haddad. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio would expand his lead to 49% versus 32%. Haddad faces high rejection at 58%, while Tarcísio has 38% rejection.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra sinais de fadiga eleitoral com Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows that even without Lula in the race, Flávio Bolsonaro remains at a disadvantage or in a technical tie with Geraldo Alckmin and Fernando Haddad, reflecting high rejection of the two main figures. Around 47% of voters fear Lula’s re-election and 45% fear Bolsonaro’s election, indicating electoral fatigue. The scenario suggests uncertainty, with over 40% of the electorate open to changing their vote and new candidates like Caiado, Zema, and Renan Santos gaining traction.

item.title: Quaest: ACM Neto e Jerônimo Rodrigues têm empate técnico na disputa para o governo da Bahia no 1º turno
item.description: The Quaest poll shows a technical tie between ACM Neto (Union Brazil) and Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) in the Bahia gubernatorial race for the first round, with Neto leading at 41% against Rodrigues’ 37% or 36% depending on the scenario. A potential second-round matchup is also tied (41% to 38%), and Rodrigues has higher rejection (42%) than Neto (32%).

item.title: Quaest: Tarcísio tem 38%, Haddad, 26%, Kataguiri, 5% e Paulo Serra, 5% na disputa para o governo de São Paulo
item.description: A Quaest poll released on April 29 shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 38% in Scenario 1, followed by Fernando Haddad (PT) at 26%, Kim Kataguiri (Missão) at 5%, and Paulo Serra (PSDB) at 5%. In a simulated runoff, Tarcísio leads Haddad 49% to 32%. The survey of 1,650 voters conducted April 23–27 has a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Tarcísio tem piora na avaliação, mas venceria Haddad em disputa em SP
item.description: According to a Genial/Quaest poll, Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) shows worsened approval ratings but still defeats Fernando Haddad (PT) in all first- and second-round scenarios for the São Paulo gubernatorial race. The survey was released on Wednesday, April 29, 2026.
